title: Introduce dynamic column compression and tactile resize rails for large virtualized tables
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Design an interaction pattern and visual affordance that allows users to resize columns in extremely wide virtualized tables with minimal layout thrash, predictable snapping, and an optional compression mode that reduces adjacent column widths to preserve table width without forcing horizontal scroll. This includes a new tactile resize rail (a persistent visual rail that surfaces on hover/focus) and a 'dynamic compression' behavior that isolates content overflow to lower-priority columns.

Background: Current column-resize behavior in the component library causes janky layout shifts for large result sets (especially with virtualization). Teams want both fine-grained control for power users and a compacting behavior for dense screens (dashboards, logs). Existing tickets focus on resizing, density tokens, and virtualization separately; this ticket unifies them into a single UX that is resilient to virtualization and accessible for keyboard/screen reader users.

Scope and deliverables:
- Interaction spec for tactile resize rails (hover/focus affordance, persistent rail mode, drag handles).
- Compression algorithm spec (priority-based shrink, min-width enforcement, snap thresholds, Overflow indicator).
- Accessibility: keyboard resize via arrow keys + modifier, live region messages for SRs, focus states.
- Visual tokens: new token set for rail thickness, hover color, compression overlay opacity, and snap micro-animation.
- Prototype: lightweight React prototype demonstrating behavior on large virtualized list with 10k rows.
- Engineering handoff doc with performance constraints and recommended implementation hooks (transform-based column offsets, measurement cache, requestAnimationFrame batching).

Acceptance criteria:
1) UX flows documented with annotated Figma file and click-through prototype.
2) Prototype demonstrates resize without layout jank at 10k rows on a mid-range laptop.
3) Compression algorithm preserves min-width tokens and exposes a per-column 'priority' attribute for shrink ordering.
4) Keyboard and screen reader interactions are documented and tested with simple a11y checklist.
5) Design review sign-off from PM and two engineers; follow-up engineering tickets created for runtime APIs.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We avoid forcing engineers to rework the serving runtime; prefer adding hooks that sidestep per-row reflow (e.g., use column transform offsets and clip masks).
- Compression must be deterministic across browsers; this requires a well-defined tie-breaker for equal-priority columns.
- Visual density tokens must remain backward-compatible; introduce new tokens as opt-in so existing tables are unaffected.
comments: 2025-02-28 - Aisha Khan: Initial ticket created after cross-team sync. Noted heavy customer interest from platform console dashboards wanting compact logs view.
2025-03-01 - Marco Chen: Engineering constraints added — prefer transform-based layout updates to avoid reflow. Will prototype a minimal React demo to validate. Assigned estimate 5.
2025-03-02 - Priya Patel (PM): Request to add a per-column toggle to opt out of compression for critical columns (ID, timestamp). Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-03 - Design crit: Feedback from design review — rails should be visible on hover + persistent mode in dense mode. Add micro-interaction for snap feedback (8px pulse). Also clarify keyboard modifiers for coarse vs fine resize.

2025-03-04 - Usability test (5 participants): Findings - compression mode is intuitive for reducing horizontal scroll, but users wanted clearer indication of which columns will compress first. Action: introduce a subtle gradient overlay on candidate columns and a tooltip explaining priority ordering.

2025-03-05 - Marco Chen: Early prototype shows 3x fewer layout paints by using cached measurements and CSS transform translateX for columns; still need to validate with virtualization windowing library (react-window/react-virtualized). I opened ENG spike ENG-19250 for perf instrumentation.

2025-03-06 - Accessibility review (Liam O'Connor): Keyboard resize model OK; suggest announcing "Column X resized to N pixels" using aria-live polite. Also recommend a focusable rail target to avoid relying solely on hover for discoverability.

2025-03-07 - Aisha Khan: Updated ticket with new token names (table.rail.width, table.rail.hoverColor, table.compress.overlayOpacity) and added link to Figma prototype. Next: finalize visual tokens and create handoff doc for engineers.

2025-03-07 - Marco Chen: Planning to break implementation into three engineering tasks: resize-rail component, compression algorithm + API, and virtualization performance integration. Will create PRs after design handoff.
2025-03-07 - Follow-up tasks: schedule micro-usability test for keyboard interactions; produce GIFs for the PR description; include telemetry points for user-initiated resizes.
